result:
I ran the full review of DG7 candidate `sha256:33266ccd…` (source `152db5b51`), and my verdict is **FAIL**. The cause is one new Medium finding. Nothing Critical, High or mandatory is open. This is an engineering review only: it grants no G1–G6, Finance, IT or production approval, and product G6 does not imply DG7.

The candidate recomputed identically (3158 files, empty manifest diff) at the start and the end. HEAD (`1c119c031`) differs from the source commit only by the assignments, manifest and `stages.json`. Everything ran in disposable clones, which I removed at the end. Apart from deps:verify (registry residual, recorded as PASS on the offline surface), the only checks recorded FAIL are the four behind the findings and the reopened verification. Every failure that appears in a log I cite is explained in the record.

**Re-run on this candidate:**
- **Static and unit:** build, typecheck, lint, OpenAPI lint, no-CDN and prettier exit 0. Unit tests pass in both locales. One unit file needs a handback file my sparse clone leaves out; it passes 6/6 in the main repository.
- **Integration:** 475/475 files, 4696 passed. There are two new teardown-race error lines in one test file under heavy load. Product code is unchanged since round 1 and all 5 tests in that file pass.
- **e2e, English and Arabic:**
  - Product journeys: 572 passed. The 2 demo-only skips pass on the demo stack.
  - Root acceptance specs: 288 passed, all connections loopback.
  - Demo specs: 10/10.
  - Arabic screens are right-to-left, English left-to-right.
- **Acceptance scenarios and drills:**
  - A18 on one archive: verify 7/7, drill D0–D11 PASS, harness 10/10.
  - Offline drill: 10/10.
  - A19 without containers: checks R1–R9 PASS, harness 13/13, backup tests 13/13.
  - A06 bundle replay: 28/28.
  - Production init and data dictionary pass.
  - A26 regression: 7/7.
  - A27 re-drill: passes, including the K11 clause.
- **Tool tests:** pass apart from six known sparse-clone failures, which pass in the main repository.
- **Delivery records and handover:** historical validation DG0–DG6, secret scans, handover tools and the protocol audit (279 hits, the same as the orchestrator's report) all pass.

**Verifications (`qa-verifier.verifications.json`):**
- **F-DG7-1021: PASS, CLOSED_VERIFIED.** The ADR-0071 amendment matches the release-notes generator on every point I checked.
- **F-DG7-1022: FAIL, REOPENED** (Low; not blocking on its own). The only change is the D-282 note in `decisions.md`. The register and release notes are unchanged, and the REQ-DLV-014 clause still promises old-branch findings "shown by validate --stage DG7", which D-282 itself says cannot be shown. The assignment allowed only CLOSED_VERIFIED or REOPENED. Accepting it as an observation would need the release-auditor to agree as well.

**New findings (`qa-verifier.findings.json`):**

| ID | Severity | Owner | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F-DG7-1051 | **Medium** | devops-engineer | The Compose half of A19 (the backup profile on postgres:18, the three steps in `backup-restore.md` §3.2, and a restore into a second Compose project) has never been run in any DG7 evidence. The orchestrator's host run does not include it. DO-D11 changed that sequence without running it. The guide still says it "is recorded" on the orchestrator's host, and the release notes list no blocker, although the plan says an unrun half is a disclosed release blocker. |
| F-DG7-1052 | Low | solution-architect | ADR-0063 (secret-scan exemption) and ADR-0066 (backup-time checks) were not amended for the DO-D11 repairs. DO-D11's questions Q1 and Q2 about this have no answer. |
| F-DG7-1053 | Low | devops-engineer | `backup.sh` refuses a symlink to an owner-only backup directory, with the misleading message "writable by group or others". It fails safe, and passing the resolved path works around it. |

I missed F-DG7-1051 in round 1, when the same gap already existed. The other round-1 findings, D-282's widening of the finding-ID pattern, and the other disclosures I was asked to judge are covered in the record (checks QA-RG2-29 and QA-RG2-30). I judged the widened ID pattern sound.

**Two contradictions in the assignment:**
- **Round number:** it asks for `round: 7`, but the validator requires the record's round to match its directory, so I recorded round 2.
- **Q19 row count:** it says 18 DG7 rows rely on the Q19 extension; I count 23, which matches round 1 and the release notes.

Two other reviewers' records were auto-committed into the repository during my run. I opened none of them.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG7/round-2/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.findings.json
- qa-verifier.verifications.json
- qa-verifier.md

The logs, scripts and screenshots are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/qa/round-2/`.
